findings.claim: The observed window is the native score clock [0.0, 0.49] with 50 observed score nodes and learning support [0.0, 0.5]; recorded affinities were removed and the score prior is equal, so selection preference is the only available label and decoded final affinity is unobserved.

The landmark_00_soft_mass curve over the observed support is non-monotone: it rises from about -0.37 z at t=0 to a peak near +1.64 z around t=0.16, then declines to about -0.28 z at t=0.49, with first-node rate z=+9.27, last-node rate z=-10.00, 4 sign changes and 1 strong sign conflict across 14 independent batches; the cubic polynomial was not accepted (relative node RMSE 0.286) and extrapolation is disallowed.

hypotheses.direction: no fixed direction; the contrast reverses, so any temporal blend should be evaluated against the reversal rather than a constant target
hypotheses.falsifier: a re-read of the same curve showing a single consistent sign of the node-to-node rate across the window, or an accepted polynomial with no sign changes
hypotheses.scope: global over the observed score window [0.0, 0.49]
hypotheses.statement: The landmark_00_soft_mass coordinate contrast reverses sign within the observed window rather than holding a stationary target, so a reward that treats this coordinate as a fixed endpoint target would be mis-specified over the full support.

limitations: Only one feature curve (landmark_00_soft_mass) was read; the remaining 199 curve features were not inspected, so no cross-feature or regional conclusion is supported.
Stage profiles and temporal profiles are unavailable; no stage boundary or data-derived knot is established.
Selection preference is association only; descendant survival, last recorded joint-head scores and decoded final affinity are not observed here, so no claim about final benefit is made.
The contrast and its time derivative do not by themselves specify an absolute coordinate target or spatial gradient; no such target is asserted.
